utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Good morning to everyone. Madam Registrar, will you please call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Case number IT-00-39-T, the Prosecutor versus Momcilo Krajisnik.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Madam Registrar. Good morning, I see that we have not a new team but at least a different team. For the record, Mr. Harmon, this morning the OTP appearances.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, good morning, Mr. President, Your Honour, counsel, Mr. Margetts is appearing with me today and we are assisted by Mrs. Javier. Mr. Margetts will take the next witness, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you. May I take it you're ready to call your next witness, no protective measures in place. Madam Registrar, thank you. Madam Usher, will you please escort the witness into the courtroom and perhaps meanwhile the office of the Prosecutor could inform us whether there's any wish to respond to the request for a certificate for an appeal on the decision on the motion for adjournment.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Your Honour, it is not our intention to file a response to that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, and not to order -- or respond either.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. Loukas.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: Yes, thank you, Your Honour. Prior to the witness coming into court, there is just a few matters I need to update from the housekeeping session late on Friday evening.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: I don't know if Your Honour would like me to go through those matters now or at a subsequent time. I'm just placing that on the record firstly that there are some matters that need to be dealt with.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Perhaps if the witness enters the courtroom, we would rather pay attention to him than to -- how much time would you need to address these matters?

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: Oh, Your Honour, I would submit something around five minutes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay. Then we'll find five minutes somewhere today.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: There is one other matter that I wish to place on the record prior to the witness giving his evidence, Your Honour, and he really should not be in court for this.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It should be done before? Yes, okay. Then Witness, could you wait for one second outside since.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, Ms. Loukas.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: Yes, thank you, Your Honours. It's just that Your Honour didn't ask me prior to ask asking for the witness to come in whether or not I had any matters just inquired of the Prosecution. Now, Your Honour, in relation to this witness, I can indicate that I will not be in a position to cross-examine this witness when he finishes giving his evidence in chief. I can indicate that I've received quite some material from Mr. Krajisnik in relation to this witness and there's a great wealth of documents and I certainly do not wish to go through the matters relating to the adjournment motion of which Your Honours have made a decision and I cannot cavil with that. We've applied for certification and there it lies, but nevertheless, in relation to this witness, Your Honour, I would submit that he would complete his evidence in chief and that he would return for cross-examination at a later stage at which stage the Defence will be properly prepared, particularly in relation to the wealth of material as I've indicated that I've received from Mr. Krajisnik and this certainly matters for which need further conferences with Mr. Krajisnik. I've indicated that I've organised for two conferences, one this afternoon and another one tomorrow afternoon but it's just not going to be adequate for the purposes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. Loukas, just a question, this is material not disclosed by the Prosecution but material you received from the accused?

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: Correct, Your Honour, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: May I just inquire, has this witness -- since when is this witness on the list of witnesses? Since when could the Defence and could the -- could Mr. Krajisnik expect this witness to testify and when have the statements been disclosed?

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: Your Honour, the statements were disclosed in January 2004, January last year.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: This witness was scheduled to immediately follow the evidence of Mr. Andic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, but he was on the list as a witness since -- from the beginning.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: Since January 2004, the material was disclosed and I don't have the specific date that he was added to the list.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: But there's not a recent change in scheduling and -- which, of course, raises an issue, Ms. Loukas, which I'll not at this moment deal with but -- and that is why any material received from Mr. Krajisnik you received it not one year ago but only recently.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: Well, Your Honour, that answer -- that question is easily answered in the sense that the material, of course, is received in B/C/S and it has to be translated and Your Honours, in relation to that, we've not had the opportunity to have that material translated in terms of the fact that we deal with our witnesses on a pretty much firefighting ad hoc as they come up basis while we're trying to balance the rest of the priorities of our case.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, it's -- you say it's easily answered. That does not yet mean that the answer would justify any delay. The Chamber will consider the matter and see whether an opportunity will be given to -- well, certainly an opportunity will be given to the Defence to cross-examine the witness and if the Defence is not ready to do that, what the consequences would be the Chamber will consider that. Mr. Margetts.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: Your Honour, on issue of scheduling, should this witness not proceed for cross-examination, of course, we wouldn't be in a position to call another witness to replace that court time. Secondly, if this application is to be maintained, in light of the circumstance of this witness, prior to him commencing his evidence here, we'd like the opportunity to speak with him and put to the Chamber the proposition that Ms. Loukas has presented to the Court and see what concerns he may have in relation to his evidence being partially completed and him returning to Bosnia. He is, again, an insider and there are certain issues that may be relevant to this decision.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. I do understand, Ms. Loukas, that meeting has been scheduled for this afternoon or for tomorrow with Mr. Krajisnik; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: That's correct, Your Honour. I have a conference with him this afternoon and tomorrow afternoon.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, and I also take it that you will need two days, Mr. Margetts, to -- for the examination in chief.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The Chamber at this moment does not consider that there's any reason to discuss what to do if the witness had to be sent home and come back again. At this moment, the Chamber invites the Prosecution to examine the witness in chief. It expects that it will take two days and after that, an opportunity will be given to the defence to cross-examine the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Usher, could you please escort the witness into the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Good morning. I take it, Mr. Djokanovic, can you hear me in a language which you understand?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I can and I wish you a very good morning too.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: First of all, apologies for asking you in and then asking you to leave again. We are now about to start with your testimony and the Rules of Procedure and Evidence require you to make a solemn declaration that you will speak the truth, the whole truth and nothing but the truth. May I invite you to make that declaration.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you. Please be seated. You will first be examined by Mr. Margetts, counsel for the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: Your Honour, there's just one matter with the ELMO, it's obstructing the vision between counsel and the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Usher, could you remove the ELMO -- I guess, put it in such a position that Mr. Margetts still can see the witness. Yes, that's better.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: Your Honour, you we won't be needing the ELMO.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Perhaps, Madam Registrar, if you move it even a bit more so that it doesn't bother anyone.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. Examined by Mr. Margetts:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Good morning, Dr. Djokanovic?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN DJOKANOVIC
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. Margetts.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Dr. Djokanovic, could you state your full name for the Court?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN DJOKANOVIC
utterances.text: My name is Dragan Djokanovic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Dr. Djokanovic, you were born in the Trnovo municipality in Bosnia on the 25th of April, 1958; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN DJOKANOVIC
utterances.text: I was born on the 20th of April, 1958 at Trnovo.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You are a qualified medical practitioner and your specialty is pediatrics; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN DJOKANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I'm a pediatrician.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In the early 1980s, were you a member of the Yugoslav national gymnastics team?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN DJOKANOVIC
utterances.text: I played for the youth and the senior representation of Yugoslavia.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: From 1990 to 1996, were you involved in politics in Bosnia and Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN DJOKANOVIC
utterances.text: I was in politics in that period, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Dr. Djokanovic, I'm just going to list to you various activities that you were involved in from May 1990 to 1994, and when I list these activities, if you could affirm whether or not how I've described these involvements is correct. In May 1990, you formed the Workers Democratic Party of Federalists and you became the president of this party.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN DJOKANOVIC
utterances.text: That's correct. On the 2nd May of 1990, you were right. It was called the Workers Democratic Party of Federalists, that's what it was called at the time.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And the name of this party was changed to the Democratic Federalist Party; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN DJOKANOVIC
utterances.text: In the summer of 1991, the party was renamed Democratic Federalist Party.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: From 1991 -- were you involved in activities relating to the preservation of the federal state of Yugoslavia and between late '91 and February 1992, were you instrumental in convening the convention on Yugoslavia?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN DJOKANOVIC
utterances.text: My entire political activity in 1990 and 1991 was a political struggle for the preservation of Yugoslavia. Perhaps as we move on, we will discuss the specific political goals but in 1990, yes, it was a struggle for the preservation of Yugoslavia and in late 1990 and in 1991, I was one of the initiators of this activity for a convention that was later on negotiated and discussed in Belgrade.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes, Dr. Djokanovic, we'll go into detail in relation to each of these engagement that you had. I just wanted to go through the listing of your activities to give the Court as to some indications of what your general involvements were in 1991, 1992. In May 1992, did you schedule the press conference in Belgrade on the convention on Yugoslavia and the constitution of Yugoslavia?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN DJOKANOVIC
utterances.text: This was the last press conference at the International Press Centre by the coordinating body that was drafting the convention for Yugoslavia, yes.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's correction, preparing the conference on Yugoslavia.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: From the founding Assembly of Serbian People of Bosnia and Herzegovina which was on the 24th of October, 1991, did you attend sessions of the assembly of the Serbian people of Bosnia and Herzegovina and did you continue to attend those sessions until the summer of 1994?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN DJOKANOVIC
utterances.text: I was mostly -- yes, for the most time, I was present at the sessions of the assembly of Republika Srpska.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'd like to present to the witness, the first nine exhibits in the order that they appear in the exhibit listing. These documents are various appointments that the witness had during 1992.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, please do so. Mr. Margetts, could you have them as a bundle, it takes enormous time to get them all separated, distribute them. If you offer them, all nine of them, then ...

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: My apologies, Your Honour, we will attempt to rectify that on the next occasion.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar, could you assign numbers. The first one is a list of employees that would have number P --

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: This will be Prosecution Exhibit P532.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The next one is a appointment of a war commission members for the Zvornik municipality by Dragan Djokanovic will be P --

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: Your Honour, just so we can ensure that we have the right exhibit. Does Your Honour have the ERN number for that one?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I have got -- the ERN number is 8672.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: Yes, thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. The next one would be the decision stamped and signed by Karadzic 17th of June 1992, that will be P534, I take it Madam Registrar?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The next one would be document number 6792 dated 16th of June, appointment of a War Commission members Vlasenica would P --

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: Sorry, Your Honour, it would be useful as Your Honour goes through these particular exhibits just to have the ERN number because there's -- there are two on the 17th of June 1992 both signed by Dr. Karadzic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, that's why I gave the numbers of the decision as well, not just the date, but the last one is 8675.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour, I'm much obliged.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The next exhibit would be the document with the number 046021 dated the 16th of June, appointment of War Commission members, that would be P536. The next one would be the document 01/13692, 16th of June, appointment of a War Commission and now about Bratunac. That would be P537, yes. The next one --

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: Your Honour, the next one in order is in fact one from the binder P64A of Pat Treanor, that's the document with the ERN 00903135.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: And then the next one in order is dated 21 July 1992 is also from that binder, P64A, that's the one 00903119.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So they do not need any numbers to be assigned because they are admitted into evidence already. The same would be true then for the third one, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So now the whole numbering -- that's what happens, Madam Registrar, if I want to proceed quickly. The number P534 I just assigned will now be given to the document I gave number 535, so that becomes 534. 536 will then become 535. 537 will then be 536. The next document is a decision of the -- with the number 018092 will not be assigned a number, it's admitted already into evidence. The next one, decision numbered or confirmation number 0133492 is admitted into evidence already. Then the last one is a decision by which Mr. Djokanovic is appointed as an advisor to the Republika Srpska Presidency and that will receive number P537. Please proceed. If this goes in a more orderly way, it really saves time.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour, and I apologise for the inconvenience and we will attempt to rectify that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Dr. Djokanovic, do you have before you the nine documents that have just been assigned exhibit numbers?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN DJOKANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I do all the nine documents.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you refer to the first document in chronological order and that is the document dated April 1992 where your name is listed ninth on that table and could you confirm that this document correctly records that you were a physician stationed at the Vrace police academy in Sarajevo in April 1992?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN DJOKANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct, but the signature is not mine.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you, Dr. Djokanovic. Could you refer to the next document, which is the appointment of the War Commission for Zvornik and could you confirm that on the 13th of June, 1992 you were appointed to the War Commission of Zvornik and I'm referring to the exhibit which is P533.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN DJOKANOVIC
utterances.text: This is a document which actually is a proposal from Zvornik for the members of the War Commission for that particular municipality.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes, and could I refer you to the next document which is dated 17 June 1992 and again records that you were proposed as a member of the War Commission of Zvornik. Could you just observe to the Trial Chamber what the difference is in the constitution of the membership of the War Commission referred to in the 13 June document and the 17 June document and that 17 June document is the document which was previously marked P529.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN DJOKANOVIC
utterances.text: The proposal which I received in Zvornik does not contain the name of Branislav Grujic but this document which was signed by Dr. Karadzic does contain the name of Branislav Grujic in number three.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could we refer to the next document which is P534 and is the listing of the members of the War Commission of Vlasenica. Can you confirm that you were a member of the War Commission of Vlasenica?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN DJOKANOVIC
utterances.text: This is a proposal for the members of the War Commission which I received in Vlasenica, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Referring to the next document which is P535 and this is a proposal in respect to the members of the War Commission of the municipality of Skelani. Again, could you confirm that you were proposed as a member of the War Commission of Skelani?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN DJOKANOVIC
utterances.text: This is a proposal for the members of the War Commission for the municipality of Skelani.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The same question again in respect of the next document, which is P536 and that's in regard to the municipality of Bratunac.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN DJOKANOVIC
utterances.text: That is correct. This is also a proposal for the members of the War Commission for the municipality of Bratunac.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Referring to the next document which is previous Prosecution Exhibit P64A, binder 26, tab 27, and that's in regard to the appointments to the municipality of Sekovici, can you again confirm that you were proposed as a member of the War Commission of Sekovici.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN DJOKANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, this is the final appointment of members of the War Commission for the municipality of Sekovici signed by Dr. Radovan Karadzic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you confirm that following these proposals for memberships to these War Commissions, you were in fact appointed to each of these War Commissions for these municipalities?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN DJOKANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. After all these nominations were made, Dr. Karadzic appointed me a member of this commission, in fact, the presiding member.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'm going to refer to the next document which is from the previous Prosecution Exhibit P64A binder 26, tab 9, and it's dated 21 July 1992 and it is the appointment -- it's the confirmation of the appointment of the members of the War Commission for Novo Sarajevo and can you confirm that the reference at point 1 to the republican commissioner is a reference to yourself?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN DJOKANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, this was signed by Dr. Karadzic, the appointment of members of the commission and number one does refer to me, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And the final document in this series is a document dated 9 October, 1992, Prosecution Exhibit P537, and can you confirm that you were appointed as an advisor to the Presidency of Republika Srpska in respect of humanitarian and information issues?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN DJOKANOVIC
utterances.text: This is a decision on the appointment of advisers to the Presidency signed by the late Professor Nikola Koljevic, it was duly recorded in the Presidency but I don't think that it was ever published in the official gazette.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Margetts, may I make one observation. If you would have asked the witness some 12 or 13 minutes ago, Mr. Djokanovic, have you been appointed this, this, this, this, have you recently seen copies of the appointment decisions in the hands of the Prosecution then of course the Defence could have easily contested that, it would have taken us approximately 40 seconds. We are now 12, 15 minutes later. I do understand that this is the traditional way of introducing information, unless, Ms. Loukas, the Defence is contesting the appointments.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: No, Your Honour, I'm not contesting.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You spent a quarter of an hour in Court on matters if the witness says, "I was appointed," if the witness confirms that he has seen copies of, then I think the Defence is fully aware if there's anything to be said about it, they can just show the document and ask further questions. That would have been -- that's already -- that's some 35 per cent of the time we used in court today. Please proceed, Mr. Margetts.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: Apologies, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Apologies, yes, if you find a way of doing these matters more efficiently, that would certainly help both the Prosecution's office itself and the Court and the Defence. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. We will proceed in that manner and we will attempt to liaise with the Defence to ascertain in advance what it is they contest and what they do not contest.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Dr. Djokanovic from July 1992 to January 1993, did you advise the Presidency of Republika Srpska in relation to effectively the establishment of Republika Srpska and the relationship between the various organs in that republic?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN DJOKANOVIC
utterances.text: In that period, I was practically working in the Presidency of the Serbian Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina with all these decisions based on all these decisions, the appointment to the War Commissions, chairman, and also my appointment to the -- as advisor to the Presidency.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: From January 1993 to spring 1994, were you the minister of war veterans' affairs in Republika Srpska?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN DJOKANOVIC
utterances.text: [No interpretation]

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: I'm sorry, I did translate.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN DJOKANOVIC
utterances.text: I was the minister for war veterans and civilian victims of war in the government of Republika Srpska.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We now received the translation. Please proceed, Mr. Margetts.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Dr. Djokanovic, when you formed the Workers Democratic Party of Federalists, what was your political platform and can you describe that political platform to the Court?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN DJOKANOVIC
utterances.text: In principle, this was a democratic party of modern orientation and the two designations in its titles, workers and federalists were the two main objectives of the party workers party because in the future after the privatisation of socially-owned property, it was committed to the giving of shares of such companies to workers and the other designation actually showed that the federalist designation that we actually called for the remaining of Bosnia and Herzegovina in a democratic federation. We wanted the constituting of a multiparty federal parliament in a federal future Yugoslavia. That was the main objective.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What was your party's position in relation to an independent Bosnia and Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN DJOKANOVIC
utterances.text: We were against the independence of Bosnia and Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What did you think the Serbs would face in an independent Bosnia?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN DJOKANOVIC
utterances.text: This entire path to the independence of Bosnia and Herzegovina was paved with difficult problems and in my view in the end it had to result in war and in an independent Bosnia and Herzegovina, the Serbs lost what they had in the federal republic of Yugoslavia and namely that they were a part of the entire Serbian people in Yugoslavia, they were constituent nation in Bosnia and Herzegovina with federal ties with other nations -- with other parts of the Serbian nation in the other parts of Yugoslavia.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'd like to present the next exhibit to Dr. Djokanovic which is the next exhibit in order, Exhibit 10.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar, that would be number?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That will be Prosecution Exhibit number P538.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Dr. Djokanovic, you have before you a press article and on the first page, there is an interview with Alija Izetbegovic and on the second page there is an interview with Adil Zulfikarpasic. I would like to refer you to a section that has been highlighted by yourself, I believe, and underlined where there's a reference to comments that Mr. Izetbegovic made in Krajina and Mr. Zulfikarpasic says that without consulting him, Izetbegovic said that if Slovenia and Croatia were to leave Yugoslavia, we would declare independence for Bosnia and that the Muslims would defend it with arms. Is that how you understood the position of the Croats and the Muslims to be?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN DJOKANOVIC
utterances.text: What you have now quoted is from Mr. Zulfikarpasic's interview but it was not he who said that we would declare an independent Bosnia and Herzegovina. He stated that it was Mr. Izetbegovic that had stated that without consulting him, without consulting Mr. Zulfikarpasic, he had said so in Krajina. He said that we, and he meant the Muslims, the Bosniaks, if Slovenia and Croatia left Yugoslavia we would declare an independent Bosnia and Herzegovina so this was what Mr. Izetbegovic had said.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What was the date of this statement from Mr. Izetbegovic?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN DJOKANOVIC
utterances.text: I don't know what exact date it was but it was at the rally in the Krajina that was 1990, that was the pre-election period in Bosnia and Herzegovina. This is the main reason why Mr. Zulfikarpasic separated from them because even though he was one of the founders of the SDA, he was man number two in that party and this is -- these are the reasons that Mr. Zulfikarpasic gives as to why he actually parted ways with Mr. Izetbegovic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In your efforts to maintain a federal Yugoslavia, what formula did you offer to the Muslims and the Croats?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN DJOKANOVIC
utterances.text: Whom do you mean specifically?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Specifically, your party and you as president of the party, what was your position as to the level of power that the Serbs and the Croats and the Muslims would have at the Bosnian republic level and the federal level?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN DJOKANOVIC
utterances.text: We worked for a democratisation of Bosnia and Herzegovina for multiparty elections to be held in Bosnia and Herzegovina for none of the three constituent peoples in the Bosnia and Herzegovina, namely the Muslims, the Croats and the Bosniaks, the three equal peoples that are three constituent peoples. We wanted to retain a democratic Bosnia and Herzegovina after the elections with equal three peoples, and for that Bosnia and Herzegovina to remain equal republic in Yugoslavia. We wanted a chamber of peoples to be introduced in the assembly instead of the existing chamber of municipalities where the key decisions would be accepted by consensus because we thought that that would be a guarantee for reserving peace and the territorial integrity of Bosnia and Herzegovina. So full equality for the three nations and full equality of Bosnia and Herzegovina within a democratic Yugoslavia.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If the Muslims and Croats rejected this option as at early February 1991, what did you consider the consequences would be?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN DJOKANOVIC
utterances.text: I'm afraid I do not understand the question. If they had rejected what? They did reject what I'm talking about.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. As at early 1991, when you were putting these positions in relation to the republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina staying within Yugoslavia, if the Muslims and the Croats rejected this proposition that Bosnia stayed within Yugoslavia, what did you think the consequences would be?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN DJOKANOVIC
utterances.text: The activities to keep Bosnia and Herzegovina within Yugoslavia in 1991 actually started in the beginning of March of that year when I called a meeting of all parliamentary and non-parliamentary parties in Bosnia and Herzegovina so that we could discuss the future of Bosnia and Herzegovina. The Serbian democratic party immediately joined in this initiative and we were practically the joint organisers of this meeting which was not attended by representatives of these Party of Democratic Action and the Croatian Democratic Union, so from the very beginning they not want to talk at all about Bosnia remaining a part of the federal Yugoslavia.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did your party establish a close relationship with the SDS?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN DJOKANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, in the second half of 1990, especially after the elections, meaning from the end of 1990 and in the course of 1991, we practically worked together on all political initiatives.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In February 1991, was there a meeting of the SDA in the region of Bihac and was there a rally where Izetbegovic made a speech?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN DJOKANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, in the mentioned period there was a huge rally in the Cazin Krajina at which Mr. Izetbegovic spoke and for the first time, the broader public could see the flags of the Muslim Croat flags tied up together, balled up together, namely the flags of the followers of the SDA and the CDU. After this meeting in Krajina, I gave an interview to the -- to Mr. Zivkovic who was a journalist of Oslobodjenje from Sarajevo and there I said that such a policy of Mr. Izetbegovic has actually led to a disruption of the there to quite harmonious relations in Bosnia and Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you tell the journalist that the actions of Izetbegovic were a route towards war?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN DJOKANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: After you gave that interview, did your relationships with the SDS -- did your relationship with the SDS become closer?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN DJOKANOVIC
utterances.text: At any rate, during 1990, this sort of curve of our relations was an upward one. Our relations were better and better and grew friendlier and friendlier.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In respect of the issue of the preservation of Yugoslavia, were the politics of Slobodan Milosevic's SPS party similar to the politics of your party?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN DJOKANOVIC
utterances.text: As officially stated in the programme of the Socialist Party of Serbia, what is officially stated there is practically identical to that of the Bosnian Federalist Party as regards the equality of citizens and the equality of the republics in the former SFRY.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you receive full support from Milosevic?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN DJOKANOVIC
utterances.text: In 1990, Milosevic came to Sarajevo twice in his capacity of president of Serbia. These were the official meetings of the presidents of the republics with members of the state Presidency and after those meetings, Milosevic would meet with a number of people who were prominent politicians in the Serbian community and once I was invited by Dr. Karadzic. Allegedly, Mr. Milosevic had said that he wanted to see me at one of those meetings although I had never seen him before and he said that he had noticed the activities of me and my party and that is why I was invited to that meeting.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did that meeting take place in February 1991, and if so, can you describe where it took place and who attended that meeting?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN DJOKANOVIC
utterances.text: I think the meeting was held on exactly the 14th of February, 1991. It was held in a building which, before the democratic elections had been club of the delegates of the deputies to the former assembly of the former Bosnia and Herzegovina but after the elections, it became the seat of the Serbian Democratic Party and currently, it is the building of the US embassy in Sarajevo. At this meeting was attended by the president of the SDS, Dr. Radovan Karadzic, by members of the Presidency, Biljana Plavsic. I think that Professor Koljevic was away, that he was in the USA. The president of the Assembly of Bosnia and Herzegovina, Mr. Momcilo Krajisnik was also there. Two prominent members of the academy of arts and sciences, Mr. Leovac, and Mr. Rajlovac were also there and other figures as well. I cannot remember all of them.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell the Court what the purpose of the meeting was and what Slobodan Milosevic told you?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN DJOKANOVIC
utterances.text: The purpose of the meeting was to familiarise all of us from Bosnia and Herzegovina with the course of the formal meeting between the presidents of the republics and the Presidency of the SFRY and President Milosevic actually briefed us on what had transpired at that meeting between the presidents of the republics and the state Presidency and he more specifically spoke about the political positions of the individual presidents, primarily, what affected us the most, the presidents of Croatia and president of Slovenia, Mr. Tudjman and Mr. Kucan. Mr. Milosevic told us that they were not in favour of a federation, that Kucan was rejecting any discussions of the subjects all together, that Mr. Tudjman wanted some sort of an asymmetrical federation and the president of the Presidency of the state Presidency -- Mr. -- of Bosnia and Herzegovina Macedonia, of Mr. Izetbegovic and Mr. Gligorov were in favour of a four-member federation, asymmetrical federation which would have some ties with Croatia and Slovenia, so this four-member federation which would have asymmetrical ties with the republic of Croatia and the republic of Slovenia.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did Milosevic mention to you the guarantees that were inherent in the federal constitution?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN DJOKANOVIC
utterances.text: Well, at this meeting we certainly did speak about the SFRY constitution which guaranteed equality to the republics. Milosevic was quite satisfied -- I'm trying to remember, of course, with some precision. He was quite happy with particularly the statement of Mr. Izetbegovic that Bosnia and Herzegovina would remain in a four-member federation, and that was a great relief for both him and us because we thought that something would come out of it after all and that we would preserve peace in Bosnia and Herzegovina. I do not remember that anyone was skeptical about it. It was only in the evening after Mr. Milosevic had left Sarajevo that we had an unpleasant surprise which we saw in the 19.30 newsreel on Sarajevo TV, when Mr. Izetbegovic actually stated that he could not support Bosnia and Herzegovina's remaining -- such a federation, so that everything returned to what it was, which is to say a lot of uncertainty and fear set in. A part -- a number of Muslim politicians gave very radical statements during that afternoon, attacking Mr. Izetbegovic for wanting to keep the Bosnian Muslims in this four-member federation which they called Greater Serbia. And in the forefront of such attacks was the academician Dr. Filipovic that afternoon.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Dr. Djokanovic, we'll move to the comments of Izetbegovic. I just want to return you to the question in relation to Milosevic's comments in respect to the federal constitution. You mentioned that he referred to the equality of the republics. Did he also refer to the right of self-determination that is expressed in the constitution?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN DJOKANOVIC
utterances.text: We did not specifically discuss the right of self-determination. At one point - I don't remember whether it was one of the participants in the meeting who put a question - but Mr. Milosevic stated that it was very unlikely that the Knin railway track would be a border dividing Serbs in Croatia from the rest of Croatia and that this was something that the Serbs in that area could accept with great difficulty.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'd like to refer to the next exhibit, which is number 11 in the order on the exhibit list.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar, that would be number ...

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Prosecution Exhibit 539.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. Loukas.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: Yes, thank you. Just before we move on to this next exhibit, I just notice in the second-last answer at page 23, line 17 it seems to refer to a 1930 newsreel. And I -- I don't believe that's correct in context. Perhaps that might be clarified with the witness before we move on.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. When you said, "an unpleasant surprise which we saw on the newsreel of Sarajevo to be" -- what year did you have in mind, 1990?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That's the time, 19.30 hours or, rather, 7.30 p.m.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, I now do understand. It's 7.30 p.m., yes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That was the -- that's the main newscast of the day. Time.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: Your Honour, together with the press article which is number 11 on the list, I'd like to also present the next document, which is number 12 on the list as well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar, that would be P540, I take it?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: No, Your Honour. It's P64A.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Oh, yes, yes. It doesn't need a number. Yes. Whenever I try to do it myself, it's ...

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Dr. Djokanovic, do you have the press article before you? It's a press article from Oslobodjenje from the 23rd of February, 1991. It's headed "Courtesy visit Slobodan Milosevic at the BHSDS headquarters." Does this press article refer to the meeting that we have just discussed?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN DJOKANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, this article relates to the meeting held with Mr. Milosevic at the head office of the Serbian Democratic Party.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Dr. Djokanovic, I'd like to refer you to the second-last paragraph in this article wherein there is a substantial quotation from Mr. Karadzic recorded, and I'd like to invite your comment on that quotation. I'll just read that quotation into the record and then I'll invite your comment on it. The quotation is as follows: "Asked by journalists whether there were any further discussions about Serbs living only in a common state, Karadzic replied, 'We don't see a need to talk about it. Just as it is Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. natural for it to rain, it is also completely natural for the Serbs to live in the same state. Thus, it is not possible to break up Yugoslavia; it is only possible to leave it. We are at peace in Bosnia and Herzegovina because of the federative status we have. Whoever wants anything different will have to fight for it. We are for an integral BH which would be sovereign in a future community. No more and no less so than Serbia.'" Do you recall Mr. Karadzic making that statement and can you comment on the statement and any effect that that statement may have had?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN DJOKANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I do recall this statement. I do not have a personal copy of the press clippings from Oslobodjenje. I have from another newspaper, and I remember this statement by Mr. Karadzic. This meeting was a follow-up meeting to that earlier meeting between the Presidency members and presidents of the states. This statement as it was reported here could have been an object of manipulation for the mass media and I do recall this statement as a very improper one because Mr. Milosevic having come there, did not deserve to hear such statements that might allude to some sort of political plans being forged between us representatives of Bosnia and Herzegovina and Milosevic, on the other side.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What effect did this statement of Karadzic have, in particular his statement that "Just as it is natural to rain, it's also completely natural for the Serbs to live in the same state"? What effect did that have in Bosnia and Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN DJOKANOVIC
utterances.text: The mass media in Bosnia and Herzegovina interpreted this statement to show that the Serb politicians and President Milosevic have identical views on the Serb people remaining in Yugoslavia; just as it was therefore natural for it to rain, it was equally so natural for us to remain there -- or rather, we all hold the same views in that regard.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You mentioned earlier that Mr. Izetbegovic made some pronouncements in the media after this meeting. Did his pronouncements follow the comments of Karadzic, and could they be seen as a response to it?

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: Your Honour, there's been quite a lot of leading. I, because it's not in areas that are subject to any dispute or what have you, I let it go, but really, that's not an appropriate way to elicit that sort of evidence, particularly that last question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Margetts.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: Your Honour, I accept --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Will you rephrase your question. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was there any response from Mr. Izetbegovic to the comments of Karadzic?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN DJOKANOVIC
utterances.text: This statement by Mr. Karadzic which was reported by the mass media the following day, the day after the meeting, did not have any impact on the statements by Mr. Izetbegovic during that afternoon. It was -- and this change of mind with Mr. Izetbegovic took place that very same day in the course of that afternoon, and this was reported by the electronic media; whereas, Mr. Karadzic's statement was only published the following day, midday or afternoon or evening. So it could not have had any impact on what Mr. Izetbegovic was to say. It could only take place at a later stage, that some speculations could be read in some mass media; although, I cannot recall any of them specifically and I could not tell you really who it was who used this statement malevolently.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: At this time in early 1991, did Slovenia and Croatia propose a confederation? And if so, can you describe what was proposed to the Court.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN DJOKANOVIC
utterances.text: In relation to the official policy in Croatia and Slovenia in -- at the end of 1990 there, they talked about a federation. It was -- as time moved on that federation was there mentioned less frequently. So they started mentioning a confederation, which for us Serbs in Bosnia meant that there would no longer be a federal government and a federal army that we perceived as an institution that could protect us in future.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you describe to the Court why it was you considered that the federal army would protect you in the future.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN DJOKANOVIC
utterances.text: When I say that, and whenever the Bosnian Serbs talk about this, they remember the experiences from World War I and World War II, when the peoples who we had lived with together in the same state for 50 years were the enemy in World War I and World War II. Therefore, the Yugoslav Peoples' Army was supposed to protect all the nations and under the SFRY constitution, it was supposed to preserve Yugoslavia as a whole but the individual peoples as well. In that particular period, especially in 1991 in Bosnia-Herzegovina, which had already seen the electoral campaign and rallies in Croatia, specifically in Split, where some 50,000 people gathered, allegedly, who were praising the Ustasas from World War II followed by the demolition of different monuments in praise of the victims of World War II, this all affected Serbs, who felt that if uncertain times were ahead, again Croats and Muslims would become allies which became true. As a matter of fact in the Cazinska Krajina, where the flags of Muslims and Croats were bound together and of course the constitution guaranteed protection for all the peoples, the Yugoslav constitution, that is why the Serbian people wished to remain within Yugoslavia.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you consider that those who supported Yugoslavia should be protected by the Yugoslav Army?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN DJOKANOVIC
utterances.text: That's not what I specifically had in mind. I remember the interview for Sarajevo Oslobodjenje that I said that between -- if a force between a civil war and military rule, I would opt for the military rule because it would preserve not only the state but would protect the citizens of the state. But if we speak of the Serbian people only, yes, I believed that the JNA was supposed to protect the citizens who wished to remain in Yugoslavia because it was, after all, an army of Yugoslavia.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Dr. Djokanovic, you have on the table before you, a document that is headed "Serbian Democratic Party" and marked "confidential." Could you refer to that document, and that's Exhibit P64A. It's the document headed "Steps to be Undertaken by Municipalities if Republican Organs Cease to Function."

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN DJOKANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I see the document. The document is before me. It was shown to me on several occasions while I was talking to the investigators but I had never seen it before it was shown to me by the OTP investigators. My party was an ally of the Serbian democratic party. We cooperated very closely but we did not interfere into internal political matters of each party so I'm not really privy to these issues. But I suppose had I asked from this document from Mr. Krajisnik, Mr. Karadzic, Mr. Koljevic or Mrs. Plavsic, that they would have given me a copy.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Dr. Djokanovic, could you refer to the opening paragraphs of this document wherein a detailed study of the SRBH and SFRY constitution is set out. In particular, I refer you to the first two paragraphs. The first paragraph setting out the equal rights of peoples of Bosnia and Herzegovina and the second paragraph stating that Bosnia is an integral part of federal Yugoslavia. Did you agree with those principles that are set out in those first two paragraphs?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN DJOKANOVIC
utterances.text: Absolutely so.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Following on, there's a further detailed constitutional analysis which you have previously had the opportunity to read. I'd like you to comment on it so if you could take your time to read it now or if you're satisfied you recall it, if you could comment as to whether you consider this constitutional analysis to be accurate and whether this was in accordance with your understanding of the relations between municipalities and federal organs.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN DJOKANOVIC
utterances.text: I believe that this is a proper analysis of the constitution of Bosnia and Herzegovina and of the constitution of the SFRY.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If either of the first two paragraphs were not followed, that is, that Bosnia and Herzegovina didn't remain an integral part of Yugoslavia, what did you think the consequence would be?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN DJOKANOVIC
utterances.text: In this period, I was always saying that all the different provisions in the constitution may change except for the fact that Bosnia-Herzegovina is a part of the Federative Republic of Yugoslavia. Equally so, anything could have changed in the constitution of Yugoslavia save for the provision providing for Yugoslavia to be a federation of those four republics and autonomous provinces. All the other solutions would inevitably lead to a war. That was my opinion and that's how -- and that's the course of events.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I refer to the last paragraph of this document and this paragraph contemplates the situation that would arise if, as the document describes it, republican organs ceased to function, that is, the republican government no longer had either authority or control. And it refers to support that may be available to those who support Yugoslavia. Can you refer to that paragraph and can you tell me whether you agree with it?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN DJOKANOVIC
utterances.text: In view of the time period when this was drafted, I fully endorse this. And when I say the time when it was drafted, that was at the time when Bosnia-Herzegovina was still part of the SFRY and that throughout the territory of the of Bosnia-Herzegovina, the SFRY constitution was applicable. And in any case, it was of an earlier date than the BiH constitution.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'll just refer you to the third-last paragraph and I'll just quote that to you as follows: It says, "In order to provide for the obstructed functioning of the municipality in such a situation as well as for the exercise of the aforementioned rights and obligations, the municipality must pass an appropriate document or decision by which it would proclaim that from the moment when such a document is passed, the municipality's territory is an integral and indivisible part of Yugoslavia that in its area only federal laws adapted to this situation have legal effect, that it recognises the exclusive authority of the federal organs, that's the SFRY assembly, the SFRY Presidency, the Federal Executive Council, the JNA security services, judiciary organs and so on in the area it covers. It says "this action would suspend the implementation of republican regulations in the areas of municipalities where such a document was passed. At the same time, it would give legitimacy to the activities and measures undertaken by the federal organs." Did you understand that to be correct that if the municipalities declared that they were a part of Yugoslavia, then the federal organs as listed in the final paragraph, the Yugoslav people's army, the federal secretariat for national defence and the federal secretariat for the interior and judiciary organs could be engaged to support those that declared allegiance to the federal state?

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: Your Honour, just in relation to that, if Mr. Margetts seeks an opinion from this witness, I think it would be better if the witness just read it and was asked if he agreed with the sentiments there expressed rather than the paraphrase that Mr. Margetts gives it which has its own nuances. And in my submission, that's a much more correct way of dealing with the document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Margetts.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: Your Honour, I've done my best to both quote large sections as to not provide for any nuances and also to facilitate an expeditious inquiry in relation to this document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Let's ask the witness: Have you read the last two paragraphs of this document?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Do you have any comment on it or do you agree with what's said in it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Firstly, I believe that this mark on the cover page stating strictly confidential isn't necessary. It was placed here for political purposes. It was a proper analysis of the SFRY constitution and there's no need for this to be strictly classified. I believe that those who drafted the document had some sort of a political agenda.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: My question was not whether the classification was justified or not but my question was whether you would agree or have any comments on the content of the last two paragraphs.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The last two paragraphs reflect the actual reality of the time which means that those who analyzed the constitution, in this case these were officials of the Serbian Democratic Party, they sent a message to their coalition partners, the SDA and the HDZ as to what their position at the time was. They wanted a Bosnia-Herzegovina within Yugoslavia, the SFRY constitution was valid throughout Bosnia-Herzegovina and it provided the Serbian side with the possibility to invoke the federal laws and that this could be done in those municipalities where they were in a majority, where they were in power and in this way, they were able to take decisions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: May I just ask one question in that respect? Was there any constitutional provision that provided for, say, ignoring the Bosnia-Herzegovina legislation if you disagreed with it and if you were a Serbian majority in your municipality?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] At any rate, there were those in the majority Serbian municipalities who had different views whereas the government in Bosnia-Herzegovina had the possibility to interpret the BiH constitution this way.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I'm afraid I do not fully follow your answer. To interpret the BiH constitution in what way, that it allowed municipalities to ...

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm talking about the SFRY constitution that one of the ruling parties in this case, the SDS, could have in this way interpreted the SFRY constitution and adapted it to its current political interests and to come out with a political agenda as it did and that it could warn its coalition partners of the position that it held which was the position basically presented in this document. Of course the other two ruling parties, the SDA and HDZ, were probably thinking about other such provisions that they could rely upon within the BiH constitution because for their political agendas, they had no foundation whatsoever in the SFRY constitution.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Is it true that the political aims of the two sides, that is, the Serbs on the one hand and Muslims and -- in a coalition with the Croats on the other hand, that the aims were irreconcilable and that similarly the interpretation of the constitution whether we have the BiH constitution or the federal constitution that the way this was approached was just as irreconcilable and therefore did not give a way out?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN DJOKANOVIC
utterances.text: At the time which was in the second half of 1991, their views did become irreconcilable and I felt this and in October, I wrote an article for the Sarajevo Oslobodjenje which was the most read daily newspaper sold throughout Bosnia-Herzegovina where I cautioned about this situation that if there were not to be a compromise if one party did not understand the other, if not, all the arguments are placed on the table, if not all the cards are placed on the table if the realities are not understood, that is the existence of a state and the existence of the constitution and the existence of national interests, that if they don't do so, they will lead their nations into a disastrous war that we had already experienced and I was trying to send a message to them to find a compromise to avoid such a scenario.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: By saying that you send a message to them to find a compromise to avoid this scenario, you mean that this was true for both sides if the one would not compromise, it would lead to war; if the other one would not compromise, it would lead to war as well.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN DJOKANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. I'm looking at the clock and it may be time for a break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, it is time for a break. We'll have a break until five minutes to 11.00. The valid clock is the clock in this courtroom.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Margetts, you may proceed, and at the same time, Mr. Harmon, you have not been present when we discussed the clocks in this building so therefore you might not have been fully aware that this is the binding clock from now on.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Mr. President, I wanted to inform you and the Chamber and counsel that in respect of the schedule that we have today, we have a witness scheduled for Thursday and Friday. That witness will not be able to attend these proceedings. I was informed during the break that the witness is in hospital and cannot attend. I am going to be dealing with that issue during the next break and I intend to deal with it fully at 2.15 this afternoon with my staff but -- so Your Honours are aware and counsel is aware the witness that is scheduled will not be in attendance. Likewise, we have a witness that has been identified to testify on Monday. That witness has problems that are quite serious and will be unable to attend. I can articulate more completely those issues. I will be attempting also during the break and this afternoon to try and fill the void that has been created by the absence of that witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, what would be, in your view, if everything goes as you wish, what would then be the first day you would present a witness again, would that be still this week or in the beginning of next week?

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: It's impossible, I'm told, to present a witness this week after the conclusion of the testimony of Dr. Djokanovic, simply because VWU needs a number of days to get witnesses here.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So therefore we have a few idle days this week. Ms. Loukas, I'm now addressing you. Before the Chamber was informed about this, we discussed whether or not any further delay will be granted for the cross-examination of Mr. Djokanovic. The Chamber unanimously and without many discussions decided that it would give an opportunity for the Defence to cross-examine the witness immediately after the examination in chief had been concluded. It seems that the Chamber at the same time does not consider it appropriate where such a request is pending and if there are a few idle days and if the witness could wait for one or one and a half days to be cross-examined, just for the matter of principle to deny it to you, so therefore we'll ask the witness. Could I ask you, if your cross-examination would start not immediately, rather, let's say on Wednesday morning but would start on Thursday or later on Thursday, would that cause you any problems if you could leave The Hague by Friday, Mr. Djokanovic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That would not cause me any problems and I would gladly stay, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Well, Ms. Loukas, then, you have some guidance of what to expect and I don't know how they call in this boxing, is this saved by the bell or -- but consider it that way. I want to be -- there should be no misunderstanding that the Chamber would not have the trial to be disrupted and to recall the witness later for cross-examination for the reasons you had given. So let's be happy with this at least for this witness, happy, I think. Please proceed, Mr. Margetts.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, just prior to that if I might just make a comment, I'm sure that in view of this recent development, what Your Honour has referred to as idle days will certainly not be idle for me but thank you for that, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No, of course. No, we are not sitting there and waiting until the next day comes, we are all busy enough, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: And I can indicate, Your Honour, I think I referred to having a conference at 3.00 this afternoon with Mr. Krajisnik, apparently it's not until 6.00 p.m. this evening and -- but in any event, we can deal with the situation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Please proceed, Mr. Margetts.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. Your Honour, I'd like to present the witness to the next exhibit in order, it's number 13 on the list and it's an article dated 26 February 1991.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: This will be Prosecution Exhibit P540.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Dr. Djokanovic, the document before you is an interview that was published in BORBA publication on the 26th of February, 1991. Do you recall reading this interview with Mr. Karadzic at the time that it was published?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN DJOKANOVIC
utterances.text: No, I did not read it when it was published. I actually read it in my interview with the Tribunal's investigators.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In this article, Dr. Djokanovic, there are various references to the themes that we've been discussing this morning and I'd just like to refer you to them. And I'd like to invite your comment on the positions that Dr. Karadzic enunciated. The first paragraph I'd like to refer you to is the third paragraph in the article and Karadzic states, keeping in mind this is 26 February, 1991, at the fourth sentence in, "We are now in a position to make a just division of territories and demarcation and to enable the peoples to create the states that they desire and then to achieve good-neighborly relations between them." He continues on, there's a question put, an answer to that question, then another question put in regard to the Sarajevo summit. In the course of his answer to this question relating to the summit, he is asked about present borders and he says "The present borders were not laid down either demographically or with the consent of the people. Those borders simply must be revised. It is most sensible to apply the ethnic principle. I think that we should expect the entire world to understand us in that regard. It would simply be impossible to apply the historical principle because everybody would stick to the stage in history that best suited him. Besides, the ethnic principle is the only possible way to draw new borders between the republics peacefully." Now, as of February 1991, did you regard those comments as being appropriate comments?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN DJOKANOVIC
utterances.text: At that period, this Karadzic's comment was not appropriate. It was, in principle, along the lines of the policy advocated by Mr. Izetbegovic at the rally in Bihac. The only extenuating circumstances that Mr. Izetbegovic spoke of his own accord at the rally and Dr. Karadzic spoke this in response to what Mr. Izetbegovic had said, namely he had said that -- clearly and loudly that he wanted a civil republic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What was it about the comments of Mr. Karadzic that you regarded as inappropriate?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN DJOKANOVIC
utterances.text: There were only hints at that time given in -- about the declaration of -- on an independent Bosnia and Herzegovina. It was not assembly material at that time. As yet the federal constitution was in force, the Bosnia and Herzegovina constitution was in force so at that time he should not have spoken about this matter at all. He should not have referred to territorial demarcation at all because the time was totally inopportune and the comment on the part of a man who was playing this role in Bosnia and Herzegovina and advocating and representing the interests of the Serbs in Bosnia and Herzegovina was totally inappropriate and irresponsible.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you meet again with Slobodan Milosevic in Sarajevo in June 1991 and, if so, who attended that meeting and what was discussed?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN DJOKANOVIC
utterances.text: [No interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: Your Honour, unfortunately, that answer -- the translation did not come through.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: I'm terribly sorry. I forgot to turn the mic on. That is because we are having great difficulty with the witness, and I'm turning up and down the volume. If you could please ask the witness to slow down a bit.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The interpreters ask you to slow down a bit because they have some difficulties in following you and perhaps you also try to keep at the same distance from the microphones so that they don't have to adjust their earphones. But by saying this I kept you off from giving the translation. If you'd like the witness to repeat his answer, I'll invite him to do so. This is a question for the interpreters.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: If that would be possible, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The question put to you was: Did you meet again with Slobodan Milosevic in Sarajevo in June 1991 and if so, who attended that meeting and what was discussed? Could you please just repeat your answer to that question since it was not translated to us.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, in June 1991, I also met with Mr. Milosevic. He played the same role that -- he was in the same role as president of Serbia at the meeting between the presidents of the republics and the state Presidency of the SFRY. We met at the Vila Stojcevac at this final meeting a somewhat narrower circle of people than at the February meeting. There were the members of the Presidency, the president of the assembly, the president of the Serbian Democratic Party, I myself was there, and a couple of other people. I cannot recall exactly who. The president of the -- Serbia told us about the course of that previous meeting and at that time, the war which was raging in Croatia was the topical issue. We talked about the possibility of the war spilling over to Bosnia and Herzegovina from Croatia. And this he said in response to a question directly put to him by Dr. Karadzic. He said, "Our people are afraid that the war from Croatia might spill over to Bosnia and Herzegovina." And Milosevic said, "As things stand now and given the political initiatives that we have now, there are slim chances that this will indeed happen and the war will spill over to Bosnia and Herzegovina from Croatia." When Mr. Izetbegovic is in, Kiro Gligorov's initiatives were launched about loose, more loose status of the republics, of these four republics relative to Serbia and Montenegro.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: Thank you, Dr. Djokanovic. Your Honour, I'd now like to play a telephone intercept to the witness and that's the next marked exhibit which is Exhibit 14 on the list and it's dated 13 August, 1991.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: And Your Honour, the CD will be tendered later.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: The CD will be Prosecution Exhibit P541 and the transcript will be P541A.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And then the translation to English, 541A.1, I take it, Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That's correct, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed. Perhaps it was unnecessary to add this because all the other documents, of course, as a general rule .1 is the translation from the original language.
