Radovan Karadzic: There's ... Dragan Djokanovic: Radovan Karadzic: No problem. They can change it. Dragan Djokanovic: All right. About the security around Tuzla, we just have to warn them, right. Radovan Karadzic: Well, we'll see to it that as well have ... Dragan Djokanovic: All right. Radovan Karadzic: And they should be provided by the party. Dragan Djokanovic: The party should provide them? Radovan Karadzic: The party should provide 20 to 30 young men to stand around and all that. Dragan Djokanovic: All right. So it is at 1900 hours tomorrow at the sports hall. Radovan Karadzic: Fine. Dragan Djokanovic: Well, then we are expecting you. Radovan Karadzic: Fine. Thank you. Dragan Djokanovic: I'd like to ask you, when do you expect to be here? Radovan Karadzic: Well, I don't know, at around 6.30. Dragan Djokanovic: Oh that's great. Your executive committee chairman would like to have a word with you. Radovan Karadzic: Put him through. Dragan Djokanovic: All right, then. Bye. Radovan Karadzic: All the best. Jovo Ivanovic: Hello. Radovan Karadzic: Yes. Jovo Ivanovic: Hello, Mr. President. My flame is Jovo Ivanovic and I'm the executive council chairman ... Radovan Karadzic: Yes. Jovo Ivanovic: ... municipality. Radovan Karadzic: Good afternoon. How do you do. Jovo Ivanovic: Well we are here, the core members and Dragan and we are getting things ready for tomorrow night. I don't want to discuss that. You probably know how long the forum will take. It's very difficult to say, about an hour or two; is that right? Radovan Karadzic: Around an hour or and a half to two, that's right. Jovo Ivanovic: Right. And what we wanted to ask is, will you and the others who come we'll of course include the MBO in this and so on will there. Radovan Karadzic: Yes. Jovo Ivanovic: Would you have time and would you be in the mood for a dinner party? Radovan Karadzic: I really don't know. Believe me, I don't think it should be anything special. Jovo Ivanovic: Well, it doesn't have to be special, just a few of us at some ... it could be at our hotel in Zvornik, I mean it doesn't have to ... Radovan Karadzic: I really don't know. You be the judge and then we can decide ... Jovo Ivanovic: Yes. Radovan Karadzic: Nothing special. You book a table but they shouldn't prepare anything special and then we'll see. It depends on the atmosphere, the number of the people and so on. Jovo Ivanovic: All right, fine. Radovan Karadzic: Fine. Jovo Ivanovic: That would be all. Radovan Karadzic: Good. See you tomorrow. Jovo Ivanovic: Right. Fine. Good-bye. Radovan Karadzic: All the best.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I take it that the written transcript has been compared with the written spoken and whenever there is any comment, please let me know. Please proceed, Mr. Margetts.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Dr. Djokanovic, do you recognise the voices on this tape?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN DJOKANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes this is a telephone conversation between myself and Dr. Karadzic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is there a third speaker on this tape?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN DJOKANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, Jovo Mijatovic, the chairman of the executive board of the Serbian Democratic Party and the municipality of Zvornik also participated at the talk. Jovo Ivanovic, that is.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Dr. Djokanovic, where were you calling Mr. Karadzic from and where was Mr. Karadzic?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN DJOKANOVIC
utterances.text: Karadzic was in Sarajevo, probably at the office of the SDS seeing that the secretary, a female voice responded from the office of the SDS and I called in from the offices of the SDS Board in Zvornik, municipal board in Zvornik.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you recall having this conversation with Dr. Karadzic?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN DJOKANOVIC
utterances.text: I do recall the conversation itself and the cause for the conversation.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you describe to the Court what the cause for the conversation was and what it was you were organising in Zvornik?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN DJOKANOVIC
utterances.text: This was the summer of 1992, the second half of summer. From the beginning of 1992 and in 1991, the political situation in Bosnia and Herzegovina kept exacerbating daily. So I thought that we could perhaps dampen these tensions by conducting talks on a compromise or compromise-based talks between the representatives of the Serbian political echelons and those of the Bosnian political echelons in Bosnia and Herzegovina, namely representatives of the Muslim Bosniak Organisation that had been founded by Mr. Zulfikarpasic who had been the first vice-president of the Party of Democratic Action, who we have already mentioned at the beginning of our talk today. And its president was the academician Mohammed Filipovic. So they supported this initiative on talks about the Serbian and side on the future of Bosnia and Herzegovina. And I used this opportunity of being in Zvornik where I worked as a doctor to get -- and was able to liaise with many honourable and renowned people, Serbs and Muslims in this city. Zvornik in fact is a city which is known as a Muslim Serbian city because it is at the very border with Serbia. So I thought if we could strike a compromise there, reach an agreement there, this could sort of spill over to the rest of Bosnia and Herzegovina. What we heard in the telephone conversation were agreements about meetings, so I called Karadzic to confirm that he would attend the cinema hall -- rather sports hall that we were preparing in Zvornik for our guests.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Djokanovic, may I invite you to look at the screen and wait until the text stops moving because you are speaking at a speech when the interpreters cannot follow. So you see it's moving. If you now and then, especially if there are longer answers, wait and then you'll see that it stops moving and then continue. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HANOTEAU
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would like to ask the witness what he means exactly when he talks about the political situation in Bosnia, B and H. What exactly does the witness mean when he says that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, they were worsening, as I said, by the day. I have already referred in my previous statements that from the rally in Cazin Krajina where Mr. Izetbegovic advocated for a civil republic and where there had been the tied-up flags of the SDA and the HDZ. And after that we saw Mr. Karadzic talking about territorial delineation, demarcation. So this was the daily dynamics that we had. We had one party advocating independence of Bosnia and Herzegovina, a civic state without the quality [as interpreted] of the people being emphasised, whereas the Serbian side said that this would not at all be carried out smoothly, that we will be identifying our territories, that we have a fulcrum in the constitution of the SFRY et cetera. So all of this taken together looked as something that could indeed lead to disastrous consequences. And that is why in 1991 I worked hard in order to avert the war if at all possible. And this meeting in Zvornik was actually called with that in mind.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HANOTEAU
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Were these discussions actually held between politicians at a higher level of the political world or were they discussions that were discussions exacerbated by the situation?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] A lot of it was the product of the situation that obtained by the politicians were following closely what was transpiring in the field and they really tried hard to respond to the exigencies of the times. So I also had the meeting, a panel discussion held in Sarajevo, in the centre of the city attended by Dr. Karadzic and Professor Koljevic, Mr. Krajisnik as guests. Also with the objective of warning the citizens in Sarajevo of the possible outcome of such an aggravated political situation or such harsh politics, rather. Dr. Karadzic spoke at this discussion that saying that he was afraid that the Muslim side was trying to push through the assembly, the declaration on independence of Bosnia and Herzegovina. This is a document that marked the whole first half of 1991 and we, the more benevolent ones were warning, were actually saying that Bosnia and Herzegovina had its own constitution that also stressed its indivisibility, territorial integrity and the right of the peoples to equality. So what was happening was along these lines with events actually succeeding one another.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HANOTEAU
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: Yes, sorry. Before the questioning proceeds, just in relation to line -- page 47, line 15, what's in the transcript there is "quality of the people" I think it should be "equality of the people."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You know the transcript will be worked over in the evening. Mr. Margetts, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Dr. Djokanovic, at this meeting in Zvornik, did you make any progress in your discussion with Zulfikarpasic in relation to your idea of Bosnia staying within federal borders?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN DJOKANOVIC
utterances.text: This rally, this meeting was -- very many people turned out at this meeting. The cinema hall was full in Zvornik. Karadzic and Koljevic and Zulfikarpasic were met with applause on the part of the audience. It all passed very calmly. The talk there was sincere. After the meeting we did not remain in Zvornik but the three of us stayed in a place called Tisce, stayed overnight in Tisce, which is a place in the direction of Kladanj and we discussed everything in some detail. I believe that Mr. Zulfikarpasic, actually, was very subtle in his understanding of the situation of Bosnia and Herzegovina and had he -- had we been fortunate enough for him to have been the leading politician of the Muslim party and conducting the Muslim policies at that time in Bosnia and Herzegovina, that war would have been indeed averted.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was Slobodan Milosevic made aware of the results of your discussions with Zulfikarpasic and did he support the proposals that you Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. were putting to the MBO?

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: Your Honours, I --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. Loukas.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: I will make a general observation in relation to the style of questioning of Mr. Margetts of which this is but one example. It really would be better just to ask a question. We do have a lot of these double-barreled questions and in my view, it's inappropriate to roll the questions up in this way.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Perhaps, Mr. Margetts, perhaps it's better to split it up. The first question is whether Milosevic was informed about it and then what his attitude was towards that. I think that's more appropriate way of dealing with it and of course -- yes, I think that would satisfy the Defence and the Chamber to frame this in an appropriate way of proceeding.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Dr. Djokanovic, was Slobodan Milosevic made aware of the discussions that you had with Zulfikarpasic and the results of those discussions?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN DJOKANOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Milosevic didn't know about this particular meeting in Zvornik. It had been agreed between Mr. Karadzic, Mr. Zulfikarpasic and me myself. And it was only the closest associates of Mr. Zulfikarpasic and Mr. Karadzic that knew about this meeting as well as, naturally, the activists of the SDS in Zvornik who informed the citizens of Zvornik about this meeting and the Municipal Board of the MBO in Zvornik. But I do recall that the media in Serbia widely covered this meeting after its holding [as interpreted] and it was obvious that Serbia was supporting such an initiative. Those days, Mr. Zulfikarpasic and Mr. Filipovic were guests visiting Belgrade and as far as I know, the president of Serbia also received then Mr. Milosevic and they spoke in detail, in fact, about some things. Namely, they said that if the Muslims from Bosnia and Herzegovina did not -- if they wanted to remain in Yugoslavia, they opened wide the door for every conceivable agreement between the Bosnian and Serbian peoples so that something specific was also proposed to the Muslims and -- Muslim side. The proposal was to the extent you give power to the Serbs in Bosnia and Herzegovina to that extent you will have like powers in Belgrade. In fact, the president -- it was also proposed that the president of the SDS, Mr. Izetbegovic, could be the president of the first such assembly and that Mr. Zulfikarpasic could be one of the presidents of the chambers of such an assembly. So they also sought to inform the wide audience, the wide public in Bosnia and Herzegovina that these were not behind-the-scenes actions but that this was something which actually reflected the needs of the time and it was in the joint interest.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'd like to move to the next exhibit which is another intercept and I'd like to play that intercept. At the same time I'd like to present the witness with a text from Oslobodjenje of 3 October 1991. They're Exhibits 15 and 16 on the list.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Mr. Margetts, will you be providing a CD additionally?

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: Yes, we will be providing a CD of the intercepts we present today.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, all the intercepts on one CD, I do understand.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: The next exhibit will be P542. And the text written by Dragan Djokanovic, P543.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Radovan Karadzic: Yes. Dragan Djokanovic: Good morning. Radovan Karadzic: Good morning. Dragan Djokanovic: Dragan Djokanovic on the line. Radovan Karadzic: Oh, got morning. How are you? Dragan Djokanovic: Tell me, are you all right? Radovan Karadzic: I'm fine, thank you. What are you doing? Radovan Karadzic: All right. Excellent. Dragan Djokanovic: That is excellent. It was time, finally, to do such ... Radovan Karadzic: Is it excellent?
